Definition: Integration of company registration, business licensing, tax compliance, regulatory compliance data
Comments: Business Registration Service (BRS) is fully integrated into eCitizen portal. National ID (Maisha Namba) required and used for business registration; owner details auto-populate from ID. All business registration services accessible online via eCitizen/BRS portal. Business registration certificate downloadable digitally. Integration between BRS, KRA (tax), and NIA (ID) is operational.

Definition: Integration of CRVS data (births, deaths, marriages) into data exchange for real-time verification and service eligibility
Comments: Maisha Namba integrates civil registration (birth) and national registration databases. The Maisha Integrated Database serves as a population register integrating primary, secondary, and tertiary registration agencies. Newborns are assigned Maisha Namba (UPI) at birth linked to birth certificates. eCitizen provides birth certificate issuance as an integrated service. The system uses a centralized hub-and-spoke model with biometric master database. Kenya Citizens and Foreign Nationals Management Service Act 2011 provides legal framework.

Definition: Integration of learner records, academic credentials, enrollment data, and scholarship/bursary systems
Comments: Maisha Namba (UPI) is directly linked to NEMIS (National Education Management Information System) for school enrollment and education records. Newborns receive Maisha Namba for future school registration. Maisha Namba is described as a 'digital shadow' tied to educational enrollment. eCitizen provides education-related services. NEMIS integration is explicitly documented as part of the Maisha Namba system design.

Definition: Integration of voter registration data for identity verification, demographic analysis, and service delivery targeting
Comments: The Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) manages voter registration. Maisha Namba (UPI) is intended for use across government services including electoral registration, but specific operational integration between IEBC voter register and a national data exchange is not documented. The Registration of Persons Act links national ID to voter eligibility but no API-level exchange documented.

Comments: NSSF (National Social Security Fund) is tied to Maisha Namba. Some employment services accessible through eCitizen (e.g., NSSF, work permits). Definition: Integration of health records, patient registration, immunization data, and health insurance into data exchange
Comments: KeHMIS project developed an interoperability layer (OpenHIE framework, HL7 standards) connecting 8 health systems including appointment management, lab results, and adherence monitoring. Maisha Namba tied to National Health Insurance Fund (NHIF/SHA) - Kenyans without digital ID cannot access NHIF. eCitizen integrates some health services. Health interoperability is partially operational through multiple channels.

Definition: Integration of passport issuance and immigration control data into the exchange platform
Comments: Passport applications are available through eCitizen platform. Maisha Namba integrates with immigration data; IPS (Immigration Principal Secretary) confirmed the Maisha Number 'integrates all databases from civil registration and national registration'. Diaspora portal launched Feb 2026 integrates immigration services via eCitizen (DIIMS). Passport issuance and renewal are fully digitized through eCitizen.

Definition: Integration with national payment systems for government-to-person (G2P), government-to-business (G2B) transactions via data exchange
Comments: M-Pesa (Safaricom, 2007) is a foundational digital payment DPI used by millions for government payments. eCitizen integrates with M-Pesa for all service payments. IFMIS manages government financial transactions across national and county governments. Ghana.gov equivalent: eCitizen payment integration is operational. Maisha Namba tied to M-Pesa ecosystem. Kenya's payments infrastructure is among the most advanced in Africa.

Comments: IFMIS provides real-time financial data for government planning and budgeting, connected across national and county governments. Kenya National Bureau of Statistics (KNBS) has open data portal. The National Digital Master Plan includes data management as a core pillar. Definition: Integration of tax administration and revenue collection systems data into the exchange platform
Comments: Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) integrated with eCitizen for tax filing. Data Protection Act 2019 governs KRA's access to eCitizen data - 2023 instance of KRA seeking eCitizen data for tax compliance noted. Maisha Namba tied to tax identification/payment authentication. IFMIS covers government financial management including revenue. eCitizen tax filing is operational via the platform.

Definition: Integration of social assistance programs, grant registries, beneficiary management systems
Comments: Maisha Namba is tied to social welfare programs - without digital ID, Kenyans cannot access support programs for orphans, vulnerable children, sick, or aged. NHIF/SHA (health insurance) tied to Maisha Namba. eCitizen facilitates social protection service access. Social protection programs are integrated with the digital ID system. DPA 2019 governs data sharing for 'strategic state interests' including civil registration and public finance.

Definition: Whether primary laws, acts, or legal instruments exist that establish authority for cross-government data sharing and govern the data exchange system
Comments: Data Protection Act 2019 (in force Nov 2019) includes a data sharing code provision specifying lawful exchange of personal data between government departments. Kenya Cloud Policy 2025 (effective May 2025) mandates interoperability and e-Government Interoperability Framework alignment. Kenya Information and Communication Act provides broader framework. Kenya Citizens and Foreign Nationals Management Service Act 2011. National Data Governance Policy under development. Multiple enabling laws exist for cross-government data sharing.

Definition: Whether a detailed implementation roadmap with phases, milestones, and timelines exists for data exchange development
Comments: DPI Roadmap process was formally launched Sep 2025 but is still under development. Kenya National Digital Master Plan 2022-2032 provides a 10-year implementation framework with KPIs, strategies, and projects. KDEAP (World Bank-funded) provides an implementation framework for digital government. Cybernetica interoperability pilot (Apr 2024-Jun 2025) developed an interoperability framework document. Full DPI roadmap not yet finalized as of Sep 2025.

Comments: Kenya National Digital Master Plan 2022-2032 is comprehensive (4 pillars including Digital Government Services and Data Management). Kenya DPI Roadmap process launched Sep 2025 with Inter-Ministerial Steering Committee. Kenya Cloud Policy 2025 (effective May 2025) includes interoperability requirements. eGovernment Interoperability Framework referenced in Cloud Policy. Definition: Is artificial intelligence integrated into the data exchange for data quality, fraud detection or predictive analytics
Comments: Kenya National Digital Master Plan 2022-2032 includes AI as a strategic priority and plans an AI master plan. Kenya launched National AI Strategy 2025-2030. eCitizen platform integrates AI-driven improvements per 2024 reports. However, AI specifically integrated into data exchange for data quality, fraud detection, or predictive analytics across at least 2 systems is not yet documented as operational; plans exist but implementation is in early stages.

Definition: Current operational status of the data exchange system
Comments: Kenya has no unified national data exchange hub but has partially operational sector-specific systems. eCitizen portal (launched 2014, 22,000+ services) integrates multiple government services. Digital ID (Maisha Namba/eCitizen) operates as a Data Exchange Layer via APIs with government population registries. IFMIS is operational across national and county governments for financial data. KeHMIS (health) has interoperability layer connecting 8 systems via OpenHIE. Cybernetica piloted an X-Road-based interoperability test environment (Apr 2024-Jun 2025). DPI roadmap process launched Sep 2025 to create unified framework.

Definition: Extent to which the data exchange enables services accessible to all population groups including persons with disabilities, elderly, low literacy
Comments: eCitizen has 13+ million registered users but Kenya's population is ~55 million. Concerns persist about exclusion of marginalized groups who cannot obtain digital ID. High Court challenges to Huduma Namba raised exclusion concerns; Maisha Namba addresses some but barriers remain for those without electricity, mobile connectivity, or digital literacy. Government has affirmed no discrimination in digital ID acquisition. Improvements in progress.

Definition: Provisions ensuring national control over government data and protecting against unauthorized foreign access
Comments: Data Protection Act 2019 (Section 50): for strategic state interests (civil registration, public finance), data must be processed through servers and data centers located in Kenya with at least one serving copy stored locally. eCitizen confirmed compliant with local data storage mandate. Kenya Cloud Policy 2025 (effective May 2025) includes interoperability requirements and mandates open standards. ODPC actively enforces compliance. Strong and enforced data sovereignty provisions.

Definition: Extent to which provincial/state and local governments participate in the data exchange
Comments: IFMIS is operational across both national government and 47 county governments (sub-national). eCitizen services are accessible nationally including at sub-national level. Huduma Centres provide in-person access to digital services nationally. Kenya National Digital Master Plan targets 100,000km of fiber to all 1,450 wards. Some fragmentation remains but sub-national participation is substantial.

Definition: Whether data exchange infrastructure and services reach rural and remote areas or concentrate in urban centers
Comments: Cybernetica noted 'limited local connectivity, non-digitised records, and siloed, manual systems continue to hinder full transition'. Kenya has ~90% mobile tower coverage but rural areas face affordability and connectivity challenges. DPI roadmap (Sep 2025) specifically addresses reducing digital divide.
